text:
kevin: quick heads-up — in the rust SSE client I'm seeing partial JSON objects after an auth refresh reconnect. payloads arrive split like '{"msg": 1' then '23, "meta":...' and our parser throws.
jess: ugh. are you on the incremental parser branch or the buffered one?
kevin: incremental. behavior: on slow consumer + token rotate we reconnect and get multiple small chunks, parser tries to parse each chunk and fails. should be recoverable but we just drop the event.
sam: we hit similar in go. our mitigation was: maintain a small append buffer per stream and only attempt json decode when we detect a full object boundary. we used brace counting as a heuristic.
anya: brace counting works for simple objects but fails with strings containing braces. better to use an incremental JSON decoder if runtime provides one (python: json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode, rust: serde_json::Deserializer::from_slice with streaming iterator).
kevin: right — rust has serde_json::StreamDeserializer but integration was awkward with SSE lines. current code assumes each event.data is a complete json blob.
jess: two angles: 1) make client accumulate until an event terminator (SSE blank line) and then feed combined data to the decoder; 2) use try/except loop: try decode, if Err::Io(UnexpectedEof) then wait for more.
sam: also watch memory with accumulation. bounded buffer + backpressure: if queue length > N, apply flow control: pause underlying read or drop oldest events and emit a warning metric.
kevin: does anyone have a small rust snippet for safe incremental parse + partial json handling?
anya: here's the gist we used in go but can port. pseudocode:
```
let mut buf = Vec::new();
for chunk in stream {
  buf.extend_from_slice(chunk);
  match serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&buf) {
    Ok(val) => { handle(val); buf.clear(); }
    Err(e) => { if is_eof_error(&e) { continue; } else { log::warn!("json error, drop chunk: {}", e); buf.clear(); } }
  }
}
```
kevin: nice. for rust we can pattern-match serde_json::Error::Io(Kind::UnexpectedEof) to continue. also add a hard max buffer size and emit metric + close stream if exceeded.
jess: for SDK change: docs + opt-in config: "sse.partial_json_buffer_bytes" default 128k, "sse.drop_on_overflow" false. add metric sse.partial_buffer_overflow.
sam: test plan: repro by inserting tiny sleeps on the server to force split chunks, then validate no dropped events and memory stays bounded.
kevin: I'm going to open a small PR with the buffer + EOF handling + config flags. assigning to @jess for review. expected to be low-risk.
ci-bot: build started for kevin/sse-partial-json-fix (job #4821) :gear:
jess: thanks, please add a unit test that simulates a 3-chunk split and a slow consumer scenario. also add a note in CHANGELOG under devex client.
kevin: will do. ping me if you want to pair on the test. :thumbsup:
anya: one more thought — when using function/tool calling or long messages, prefer NDJSON (one JSON per line) at the event level; makes delimiting trivial. worth considering as a protocol option for some routes.
sam: agreed. but default needs to remain compatible. we can add an opt-in header `X-Prefer-NDJSON: 1`.
kevin: cool. I'll include a short RFC blurb in the PR description. thanks all!
